text: World War II lasted from 1 Sept 1939 to 2 Sept 1945. Germany under Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party initiated the war in Europe. Estimated deaths: 70–85 million. The Holocaust murdered about 6 million Jews and millions of other victims.
Treaty of Versailles imposed reparations, military limits, territorial losses, and war guilt after WWI.
Hyperinflation (1923) and the Great Depression (1929) destabilized Germany and aided Nazi rise.
Hitler became Chancellor in 1933, established a dictatorship, banned opposition, and expanded state control.
Germany rebuilt its army, navy, and Luftwaffe despite Versailles restrictions.
Remilitarized Rhineland (1936), annexed Austria (1938), acquired Sudetenland, then occupied Czechoslovakia.
Germany invaded Poland on 1 Sept 1939 using Blitzkrieg. Britain and France declared war on 3 Sept 1939.
Germany conquered Denmark, Norway, the Low Countries, and France in 1940.
The Luftwaffe failed to defeat the RAF, preventing invasion of Britain.
Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941; initial gains stalled due to winter, logistics, and Soviet resistance.
Systematic persecution and murder of Jews and other groups in ghettos, concentration camps, and extermination camps.
Afrika Korps under Erwin Rommel fought Allied forces before eventual defeat.
Stalingrad (1942–43) and Kursk (1943) shifted momentum permanently to the Allies.
Strategic bombing damaged German industry, transport, and cities.
Allied landings in Normandy on 6 June 1944 opened the Western Front.
Soviets advanced from the east, Western Allies from the west. Hitler died on 30 April 1945.
Germany surrendered unconditionally; VE Day celebrated on 8 May 1945.
Germany divided into occupation zones; Nuremberg Trials prosecuted major Nazi leaders; Germany split into East and West in 1949.
Heer, Luftwaffe, Kriegsmarine, and Waffen-SS were major military organizations.
Tiger and Panther tanks, Me 262 jet, V-1 and V-2 weapons were notable developments.
Two-front war, Soviet campaign failure, Allied industrial strength, bombing, shortages, and strategic mistakes.
Denazification, division then reunification in 1990, remembrance culture, and influence on international law.
